definitions.text: The cell is the basic unit of life.
The cells of bacteria, fungi, plants and some protists (algae) have a rigid non-living wall around cell membrane. It is called cell wall.
Plasmodesmata (singular plasmodesma) are the channels in cell walls that allow the exchange of molecules between adjacent cells.
All cells have a thin and elastic cell membrane around the cytoplasm. It is selectively-permeable. It allows very few molecules to pass through it while blocks many other molecules.

According to this model the lipids make a fluid-like bilayer in which protein molecules are submerged. The lipids and proteins can move laterally. Due to these movements, the pattern or “mosaic,” of lipids and proteins constantly changes.
It is the jelly-like substance that fills the inside of a cell.
Cytosol is a liquid part of the cytoplasm that includes molecules and small particles, such as ribosomes, but not membrane-bound organelles.
Nucleoplasm contains fine thread-like material known as chromatin. It is composed of deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) and proteins.
It is a network of thin tubes and filaments present throughout the cytoplasm. It consists of three parts i.e., microtubules, microfilaments, and intermediate filaments.
Ribosomes are tiny granular structures. They are the sites of protein synthesis.
It is a network of membrane-bounded channels present throughout the cytoplasm of eukaryotic cell.

Smooth Endoplasmic Reticulum (SER): It lacks ribosomes. It is involved in lipid metabolism and in the transport of materials from one part of the cell to the other. It also detoxifies the harmful chemicals that have entered the cell.
These flattened sacs, called cisternae are stacked over each other and make a structure known as Golgi apparatus.
These are small membrane-bound vesicles that contain digestive enzymes.
These folds are called cristae (singular: crista). They increase the surface area for respiration.
These are single membrane-bound sacs filled with fluid.
This outward pressure of the vacuole on the cytoplasm and cell wall makes plant cells turgid. This pressure is called turgor pressure and the process is called turgor.

After their formation, cells undergo the process of specialization or differentiation. During this process, they get special sizes, structures, and metabolic features. As a result, they become specialized.
Such unspecialized cell that has the ability to make a variety of specialized cell types is called stem cell.

fullMarks: For a fluid mosaic model answer, begin with the lipid bilayer, then explain that proteins are embedded in it and that lipids and proteins can move laterally. Include how carbohydrates are joined to proteins or lipids.
For cell wall questions, describe its support, strength, protection and shape functions, then name the layers of the plant cell wall and their materials.
For nucleus questions, name the nuclear envelope, nuclear pores, nucleoplasm, nucleoli and chromatin; explain that DNA contains genes and controls cell activities.

For lysosome and endoplasmic reticulum answers, clearly distinguish RER (ribosomes; protein synthesis) from SER (lipid metabolism, transport and detoxification), then explain lysosomal digestion and waste breakdown.
For Golgi complex questions, explain cisternae and how the apparatus modifies proteins from rough ER, packs them into vesicles, and stores or transports them for secretion.
For chloroplast questions, name the double membrane, grana, thylakoids, stroma, photosynthetic pigments, DNA and ribosomes; connect chlorophyll and light energy to photosynthesis.
For turgor pressure, write the sequence: water-filled large vacuole presses outwards on the cytoplasm and cell wall; the cell becomes turgid, helping it maintain its shape.
When a question asks you to describe a structure, draw a clear, large diagram if useful and label the named parts accurately; finish with a sentence linking the structure to its function.
mistakes: Mistake: Saying the cell membrane is fully permeable. Fix: State that it is selectively-permeable and controls which molecules can pass.
Mistake: Mixing up rough and smooth ER. Fix: RER has ribosomes and serves in protein synthesis; SER lacks ribosomes and is involved in lipid metabolism, transport and detoxification.
Mistake: Saying cristae are the fluid inside mitochondria. Fix: Cristae are folds of the inner mitochondrial membrane; the fluid-like material is the matrix.
Mistake: Describing chromatin and chromosomes as unrelated structures. Fix: State that chromatin condenses into thick chromosomes when a cell starts dividing.
Mistake: Saying plant cells have many small temporary vacuoles like animal cells. Fix: Most mature plant cells have one large central vacuole; animal cells may have many small temporary vacuoles.

Mistake: Naming only cellulose as the material of every plant cell-wall layer. Fix: Match materials to layers: the primary wall includes cellulose, hemicellulose and pectin; the middle lamella contains magnesium, calcium and pectin; the secondary wall is mainly cellulose, lignin and other chemicals.

shortTheory.question: What are the main functions of the cell membrane?
shortTheory.answer: It is selectively-permeable. It allows very few molecules to pass through it while blocks many other molecules.

shortTheory.question: What key role does the Golgi apparatus play in eukaryotic cells?
shortTheory.answer: It modifies proteins coming from rough ER and packs them into small membrane-bound sacs called Golgi vesicles.These sacs are kept in cell or are transported to exterior in the form of secretions.

shortTheory.question: How do lysosomes contribute to the cell's functioning?
shortTheory.answer: Lysosomes also have enzymes for breaking cellular wastes. They also engulf the damaged organelles and break them. Lysosomes can store certain molecules for later use.

shortTheory.question: Why are the cristae important for cellular respiration?
shortTheory.answer: These folds are called cristae (singular: crista). They increase the surface area for respiration.

shortTheory.question: How are chromatin and chromosomes related?
shortTheory.answer: When a cell starts dividing, its chromatin condenses and takes the shape of thick chromosomes.

shortTheory.question: How would you define a stem cell?
shortTheory.answer: Such unspecialized cell that has the ability to make a variety of specialized cell types is called stem cell.
